title: Running LLMs locally: Practical LLM Performance on DGX Spark — Mozhgan Kabiri chimeh, NVIDIA
talk_summary: An NVIDIA DevRel talk benchmarking local LLM serving on a DGX Spark (GB10, 128GB unified memory) using vLLM in an optimized container, measuring tokens/sec and time-to-first-token across model sizes and quantization formats. The main finding is that NVFP4 4-bit quantization dramatically improves throughput and TTFT versus unquantized models, and that memory bandwidth (not capacity) governs throughput.

takeaways.technique: Reproducible benchmark harness with versioned artifacts
takeaways.what_they_do: An orchestrator script runs every model through an identical protocol: Docker isolation, three mandatory warm-up runs, 1-second GPU metric logging, and a unique timestamped directory per run capturing full endpoint responses and metadata.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Every model run from 1.5 billion to 14 billion follows the same strict protocol. Environment isolation via Docker, three mandatory warm-up runs

takeaways.what_they_do: They compare the same model at different precision formats and find 4-bit quantized variants are far faster than unquantized ones at similar capability, making quantization format a first-class routing dimension.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the choice of quantization format is just as important as the hardware itself
takeaways.numbers: 14B NVFP4: 20.19 tok/s vs 14B base 8.40 tok/s; 14B NVFP4 3.4x faster TTFT than unquantized 14B

takeaways.what_they_do: They instrument the streaming response to timestamp the first chunk, treating time-to-first-token as the perceived-performance metric distinct from completion tokens/sec.
takeaways.evidence_quote: time to first token is the metric that defines the user's perceived performance

takeaways.what_they_do: They serve models inside an NVIDIA-optimized container so the local environment matches the data-center deployment exactly, avoiding drift between dev and prod.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I run this inside an Nvidia optimized container. This would ensure that our environment is identical to what you would deploy in a data center.
